neutral_facts.value: The deceased couple, who had set up their own separate residence, were found to have been living independently of their in-laws. The deceased woman was found murdered in a hotel room in Pondicherry with multiple stab wounds. A charge sheet was filed under Sections 302 and 498-A of the IPC, alleging that the husband, along with his parents-in-law, had subjected the deceased to dowry harassment and caused her death. The husband committed suicide shortly after, leading to the abatement of charges against him. The parents-in-law were implicated based on statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C., but the prosecution could not establish a direct involvement or common intention. The High Court discharged the parents-in-law as there was no sufficient evidence to link them to the crime.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the parents-in-law of the deceased (accused Nos. 2 and 3) were implicated in the murder due to their alleged involvement in dowry harassment and conspiracy with their son (accused No.1) to kill the deceased.

quotes.text: The Charge-Sheet does not indicate any complicity so far as the parents-in-law of the deceased (accused Nos. 2 and 3) are concerned.
It is theoretically possible that they may have abetted or conspired in the crime or persuaded their son (accused No.1) to have perpetrated the crime.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no direct involvement of the parents-in-law in the murder, and the allegations against them were not supported by sufficient evidence or direct imputation.

quotes.text: The Appellant-complainant, in his statement, had alleged that as per the plans of the three accused, accused-husband had killed the deceased due to dowry harassment.
It is not sufficient to merely make a bald statement but further catenation should exist linking all the conspirators together.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the court's role is to determine whether a prima facie case has been established to justify prosecution, and not to delve into the merits of the case at the stage of framing charges.

quotes.text: The Court is neither a substitute nor an adjunct of the prosecution. On the contrary, once, a case is presented to it by the prosecution, its bounden duty is to sift through the material to ascertain whether a prima facie case has been established which would justify and merit the prosecution of a person.
The 'ground' in the context is not a ground for conviction, but a ground for putting the accused on trial.
